# Waiver ledger — what is not covered, and under which policy

**Hand-maintained. An earlier revision of this header claimed it was generated by
`.future/cov100/gen-final-docs.py`, which does not exist in this repository - so the file was being edited by
hand while telling its readers not to. Header corrected 2026-10-16.**

The repo's policy has four categories, and each waived file must state one on the same line as its path:

* `unreachable-by-construction` — no input reaches it (needs the invariant).
* `unreachable-in-this-environment` — needs a host/fixture **this** machine cannot
  provide (needs which one). This is *not* platform-shaped: a broken filesystem, a
  full pipe, `ENOSPC`, or a race window with no injection seam.
* `attribution-artifact` — the line is a region llvm-cov attributes to a macro
  or a closing brace (needs the neighbouring covered lines as evidence).
* `platform-unmeasured` — **the line's reachability depends on another platform**,
  and that platform's CI run is the authority. Two shapes, and both are in use in
  this repo (measured):
  * (a) the line is **not even compiled here** (`#[cfg(target_os = …)]`), so it has
    no `DA` record of its own — a verified instance is `module-goal.md`'s
    `webui/server.rs` 105-110 row (the `rundll32` arm behind
    `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]`, absent from a macOS report's `DA:` records),
    and the files listed in `platform-coverage.md`.
    **The example must name the record AND the record's form.** An earlier revision of
    this bullet cited "`module-agent-core`'s Chromium rows": that record mentions
    Chromium **zero** times (the rows are in the prose-only `module-cli-tui.md`), so the
    example pointed a reader at a document that could neither confirm nor be checked for
    it. Found by REV-AGENT (its F-2 note) — the same anchoring defect class as F.48;
  * (b) the line **compiles here but only another platform's runtime makes it
    execute** — another OS's error code, capability or probe answer — e.g.
    `module-cli.md`'s `commands/doctor.rs:173,183,186-189` (the sandbox report is
    the host probe's own answer; the `Warn` arm needs `available=false`), and
    `agent/src/rpc/commands/settings.rs`'s eight rows (the only `Err` producer is
    the Windows branch).

  **The discriminator is NOT "is it `cfg`-gated".** That test distinguishes shape
  (a) from shape (b); it does not make a row wrong. The question that separates a
  real defect is **"is the line reachable here with a better fixture?"** — and then
  **"what exactly is missing?"**: another platform's behaviour
  (`platform-unmeasured`) versus a host state this platform cannot produce
  (`unreachable-in-this-environment`) versus any input at all
  (`unreachable-by-construction`). A row must name the platform **and** the
  condition that platform satisfies.

  History, because this category flip-flopped twice and the flip-flopping is the
  reason this paragraph exists: `module-agent-rpc` F-22 reclassified
  `cli.rs:195/197` out of `platform-unmeasured` on the `cfg` test (correct — those
  lines compare arguments and are reachable on any platform; a test now covers
  them), and reclassified `cli.rs:228/234-236` *into*
  `unreachable-in-this-environment` on the same test (wrong under this definition —
  they need Windows probe results and a Windows-only capability, so they are
  shape (b) `platform-unmeasured`). That unit's own F-24 then measured the working
  convention across other modules and reached the same conclusion this paragraph
  states.

The gate checks STRUCTURE only. Whether each reason is true is the reviewer's
job, and rev-rust / rev-fe are tasked to falsify them by counterexample — a
waiver that survives is evidence, a waiver that falls is rework.

## Per module

**THE RESIDUALS BELOW ARE NOT MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — DO NOT SUM THEM** (measured 2026-10-17, when
`ledger-census.py` forced a comparison of every record against this table). Three kinds of row live here:

* **whole-scope records** whose scopes do not overlap: the `agent` family's split is by subtree
  (`agent-core` = tools/llm/agent/compaction/sandbox/…, `agent-rpc` = rpc/grpc/service/session/skills/…),
  and `module-cli` explicitly **excludes** the two MCP files, so `module-cli-mcp` adds to it without double
  counting;
* **SLICES of a parent's scope**: `module-tauri-headless` sits inside `module-tauri`'s
  (`desktop/src-tauri/`), and `module-agent-llm` sits inside `module-agent-core`'s — **adding either to its
  parent would count the same lines twice**;
* **round-1 records declared prose-only** (see CLOSEOUT §5b), where this table carries a pointer rather
  than a figure.

So the "100 %" claim is made **per scope, with the scope named** — never by totalling this column. Where a
row's figure is a subset, the row says so in its own cell.

## Environment-attributed numbers (NOT waivers)

A module can have **two defensible figures for the same source**, because a residual can depend on the
**session the measurement ran in**, not only on the code. This section exists so a reader of the final
report can tell **which numbers are machine-checkable** from **which are environment attributions** —
the distinction the user gate `todo_6a850a842666` asked the closeout to make explicit.

**Rule: an environment-attributed number is never a waiver.** It says "this line is not covered *here*,
and here is the host-state difference that explains it" — and it must name a **pinned artifact from the
other state** where the line *is* covered, plus the command that reproduces the state check. If there is
no such artifact, it is an ordinary waiver and belongs under the four categories above.

### `module-tauri-appdata` — 378 and falling: the four families, and one I registered wrongly (2026-10-17)

**Current figure: 374 uncovered / 26 files = 348 WAIVED + 24 OPEN + 2 deliberate exclusions** (measured 2026-10-18, §S29; report
`/tmp/appdata-taub-s23-normalized-lcov.info`, tripwire `reconcile.py --section "S18.5"` -> 378 mentioned /
MISSING 0). The 386/367+19 I first registered is superseded.

**CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING, one turn after making it.** I registered `commands/remote_peer.rs:283-290`
as `unreachable-in-this-environment`, reasoning that "the fixture host lives in `src/remote_peer/`". The
next segment MEASURED those eight lines as covered (`284=2, 286=1 … 290=1`, previously 0 for all eight) and
its reason is right where mine was not: `remote_host/files.rs:585` is
`"" | "preview" => prepare_preview_cached(...).or_else(|_| prepare_original(...))` — **the HOST substitutes
the original bytes itself**, so a refused preview never errors at all, and the client's retry runs only when
NO download is prepared — which an unknown session produces inside the write set. My conclusion ("no
existing fixture produces this state") was right; my mechanism was wrong, and a wrong mechanism is what
makes a waiver look permanent. The lesson is the ledger's own rule: **a category without a mechanism is
unfalsifiable, and an unfalsifiable row is the one an adversarial review will overturn.**

| family | lines | category | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands/remote_peer.rs:283-290` | 8 | — | **COVERED 2026-10-17** by `a_preview_the_host_cannot_prepare_retries_the_original_variant` (an unknown session makes the host prepare nothing, so the retry runs). Non-vacuity rests on the COUNT, not the assertion: an error assertion cannot separate retry from no-retry, and the unit's delete-the-retry MUTANT passed with its first fixture — which is why the row had looked blocked |
| `commands/remote_peer.rs:301` | 1 | `attribution-artifact` | the `)?` tail of the same block (was 298 before the segment's +3 doc lines). It reads **0** while its arguments and the next statement read non-zero — the cleanest instance of this class in the campaign |
| `commands/debug.rs:114, 116` | 2 | `unreachable-in-this-environment` | `Phase::Ready` with `owns_agent == false`, i.e. an externally started agent. **No test-only phase setter exists today; a `cfg(test)` hook of the shape already present at `agent_host.rs:253` would make it reachable, and that needs supervisor authorisation under PLAN §4b.** Registered as reachable-with-a-seam, NOT as impossible |
| `agent_bridge/review.rs:289-293` | 5 | `unreachable-in-this-environment` | a TOCTOU window with no injection point (the existence check at 285-287 and the return at 289-293 cannot be separated from a test) |
| `commands/update_recovery.rs:36-38` | 3 | `unreachable-in-this-environment` | a non-test `current_exe()`: `capture()` fingerprints the TEST BINARY's build tree (measured: does not finish in 600 s), while the parameterised `capture_under` is already covered |

**The ruling itself stands, narrowed:** the write set is still NOT extended — the discipline that made me
refuse (b) is the same one that made this family's reachability a claim worth testing, and the unit found
the fixture inside its own scope once the mechanism was stated correctly. **What I got wrong was the
mechanism, and the fix was to measure it, not to extend a scope.**

**One number this module must never publish without its qualifier:** the residual is **377-378** depending
on `src/tasks.rs:142`, covered only when `mark_interrupted_runs` actually errors (a busy store); measured
`0` in most runs and `2` in the run that closed it. That line is CLOSED-by-count, not by a test name, and
its neighbours are 140=11, 141=10, 142=2, 143=8.

**A third kind of "the number moved", worth recording here** (§S26.2): `agent_bridge/client.rs:232` is a
closing brace that reads **1** in one green run and **0** in another, with the entry line `231=3` in
both and no source change - so totals can wobble ±1 between two green runs of one tree. When "the number
moved", **check for a brace before assuming a regression**; this campaign already knew about
load-dependent tests and load-dependent failure paths, and this is a third mechanism.

## Policy notes


* A file listed under an `OPEN` / `not waived` heading counts as **not waived**
  — the gate rejects it even if its path also appears in a ledger table. That
  rule exists because one delivery relabelled 17 OPEN lines as waived.
* Deleting a production guard so a line stops existing is the forbidden inverse
  of this policy: a coverage change may only ever be a *result*. rev-rust is
  tasked to read `git diff` for removed guards and demand the correctness
  argument for each.
* Weakening an assertion to make a suite green is likewise out of policy; the
  weak-test audit (`weak-test-audit.md`) and the assertion audit cover that.
